original.indicated: pr-review --adversarial design before review: amend --unrefute before build, index-keyed refutations, no spike, no plan-path classification table

issue.why_free_form: The review found 31 gaps: Phase 5 detection after a refuting build (S1), the overrule window (S2), the closed-status consumer trace (S3), the hook's Layer 2 and Layer 3 rules (S4, S13), mixed-group merges (S5, S6), stale refutations (S7), the attack field (S8), discovery and layout (S9), plan-path state (S10), schema versioning (S11, S12), the missing Workflow tool (S14), unverified Workflow API facts (S15), agent-watcher (S16), recovery (S17), guidance (S18), agent count (S19), the strap round (S20), tests (S21) and more (S22-S31).

new_outcome.indicated: Every finding accepted with the resolution sheet's fix; the frozen spec's Review resolutions table maps each finding to its section; SPK-1, TASK-9 and TASK-10 join the plan

why_new_outcome.free_form: The plan items, values and planned tests follow the resolved spec, not the draft.

original.indicated: the developer overrules a refutation with amend --unrefute before build, or (the review's fix) a post-build unrefute --reason appending one UNREFUTED entry

issue.why_free_form: Phase 3 runs merge, amend and build in one turn with no developer-facing text before build, so a pre-build overrule never happens; a post-build-only unrefute cannot add a refutation the developer wants on a review built without -a.

new_outcome.indicated: D5 anytime: a driver pipeline, refute --pr <key> <ID> --evidence (adds REFUTED) and unrefute --pr <key> <ID> (--bubble --classification C --reason R | --fix [--reason R]), both reading the built review object, any phase after build, with or without -a; amend --unrefute dropped

why_new_outcome.free_form: Developer answer; Phase 3 stays atomic and the overrule works in either direction.

changes.discovered_by: spec review (S3), following the developer's D5

original.location: Decisions D11; REFUTED as a closed status (TS mirrors row)
original.indicated: the TS closed-status mirrors stay RESOLVED / CLOSED_NO_ACTION: a refuted id is settled before waves and never bubbled

new_outcome.indicated: D11 add-refuted: the three mirrors gain REFUTED; agent-watcher and bubble-stamp versions bump; their TS tests and release rows move (TASK-10)

why_new_outcome.free_form: The mirrors must agree with review_merge.CLOSED_STATUSES once REFUTED can follow a bubble.

original.location: Decisions D12; review findings S2, S3, S11
original.indicated: an unrefute appends one non-closing UNREFUTED status

issue.why_free_form: An overruled refutation goes either to the bubble workflow or to a Phase 5 fixer; one UNREFUTED status cannot say which, so waves and the bubble path could not route the id.

new_outcome.indicated: Two non-closing statuses appended: BUBBLED (then the existing bubble path) and NOT_RESOLVED (open; the next waves plans a fixer). No UNREFUTED status.

why_new_outcome.free_form: Developer answer; append-only, the latest-status rule reopens the id.

original.indicated: TASK-1 changes _named_ids, _pending_problems, the hook's _incoherent and _closeout_reason; id_handling is not named

issue.why_categorical: second copy of the disposition rule

Without the NOT_RESOLVED rule there, an id refuted and then overruled with unrefute --fix counts as dispositioned and the Phase 5 sentinel clears before its fix lands.

changes.discovered_by: plan review (plan vs code, and planned tests)

original.indicated: _named_ids reads the latest status everywhere; a bubble entry settles an id whatever its latest status; merge_ids keeps _combine's first-record shape; the TS mirrors only gain REFUTED; bubble-stamp stamping unqualified; KNOWN_VERSIONS left implicit

issue.why_free_form: A2: bubble -> refute -> unrefute --fix left the id in bubble_up (and bubbles), so _settled_ids, wave_inputs and disposition_ids called it settled and no fixer was planned. A4: a latest-status _named_ids would drop REFUTED -> NOT_RESOLVED ids from the orphan guard and review_edit._disposed_ids. A5: amend --merge took name and summary from the kept (possibly refuted) issue, against S5. A3: agent-watcher bubbles.ts ports all_issues_dispositioned, so it needed the NOT_RESOLVED rule too. A11: memo.ts never unstamps a Decided row. A1: KNOWN_VERSIONS is single-version and tests/lib/test_review_edit.py pins 2.2.0 twice.

new_outcome.indicated: A latest NOT_RESOLVED is open regardless of bubble entries (_settled_ids, all_issues_dispositioned, bubbles.ts dispositionedOf); apply_refute drops the id from bubbles through _without_closed_bubbles and apply_unrefute --fix removes it from bubbles, bubble_up kept as history; a raw _entry_ids backs the orphan guard and _disposed_ids; merge_ids takes name, summary and fix_kind from upheld issues; the memo stamp limit is stated and its unstamp deferred; KNOWN_VERSIONS stays single-version with the test_review_edit literals moved to rmg.SCHEMA_VERSION

why_new_outcome.free_form: Each cite was checked against the code; the plan's rules now agree with the D5 pipeline in every disposition reader, Python and TypeScript, and the planned tests pin each case.

original.location: TASK-1 action (latest NOT_RESOLVED is open regardless of bubble entries)

new_outcome.indicated: _apply_bubbles and review_edit.add_bubble (TASK-4) and pr_review's bubble command (TASK-5) also append a BUBBLED resolution entry when the id's latest status is NOT_RESOLVED, so the latest status becomes BUBBLED and settles through the bubble entry

why_new_outcome.free_form: Developer chose append-BUBBLED over refusing the bubble or leaving the id stuck.
